title: Topographical Organization and Density Analysis of Substance P-IR Axons in Mouse Stomach
author: Duyen Nguyen
materials: To verify whether the SP-IR axons in the stomach originated from the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and vagal nodose-petrosal ganglia complex (VNG), mice (n=5) were anesthetized with 2-3% Isoflurane Covetrus Catalog #029404 . The depth of anesthesia was determined by absence of the hind paw pinch withdrawal reflex. Double-labeling: To investigate whether SP-IR axons in the stomach originated from sympathetic (catecholaminergic) or enteric ganglia, whole muscular walls (ventral n=3, dorsal n=3) were double labeled for SP with tyrosine hydroxylase (TH, a sympathetic marker) or Vesicular Acetylcholine Transporter (VAChT, a marker of enteric excitatory muscle motor neurons, vagal pre-enteric neurons and possibly gastric interneurons). The samples were processed using the same protocol as single labeling with the addition of either TH or VAChT sequentially to the stomach samples. The primary antibodies were: Rabbit anti-substance P antibody; AB_572266 Immunostar Catalog #20064 polyclonal, Sheep anti-tyrosine hydroxylase antibody Merck Millipore (EMD Millipore) Catalog #AB1542 (RRID: AB_90755) polyclonal, Goat anti-Vesicular Acetylcholine Transporter (VAChT) antibody Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #ABN100 (RRID: AB_2630394) ,polyclonal. Before the double labeling experiment, Rabbit anti-SP primary antibody was used to label stomach walls (n=5) which yielded a similar distribution pattern and morphology of the SP-IR axons (not shown) that had been seen using Guinea pig SP primary antibody in the single labeling experiment above. steps.title: Counterstain Neurons (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform retrograde labeling of neurons in the peripheral ganglia and the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DmnX).

substeps.instruction: Inject 0.3 ml of 3 mg/ml Fluorogold Fluorochrome (i.p.) per mouse.
Allow 3–5 days for transport before perfusion.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Perfuse Mice
steps.instruction: Deeply anesthetize mice and perform systemic perfusion to fix the stomach and brainstem tissues.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mice with 4% Isoflurane; verify depth via absence of hind paw pinch withdrawal reflex.
Cut the inferior vena cava to drain blood.
Perfuse through the left ventricle with 38-40 °C phosphate-buffered saline (0.1 M PBS, pH = 7.4) for 5 minutes.
Fix by perfusion with 4 °C Zamboni's fixative (15% picric acid and 2% paraformaldehyde in PBS, pH = 7.4).

steps.title: Harvest and Prepare Stomach Tissue
steps.instruction: Extract the stomach and prepare flat-mounts of the muscular wall.

substeps.instruction: Remove the whole stomach including small portions of the distal esophagus and proximal duodenum.
Cut the stomach open along the lesser and greater curvatures into ventral and dorsal halves.
Remove stomach contents and rinse with distilled water.
Post-fix in Zamboni's fixative for 24 hours.
Peel the mucosal and submucosal layers off the muscular wall to isolate the longitudinal muscle, circular muscle, and myenteric plexus (flat-mounts).

steps.title: Harvest and Section Brainstem
steps.instruction: Prepare brainstem sections for DmnX analysis (if Fluorogold was used).

substeps.instruction: Remove the brainstems.
Cross-section the brainstem at 100 μm relative to the obex (-1000 to + 1000 μm) using a Cryostat.

steps.title: Immunohistochemical Labeling
steps.instruction: Perform SP IHC labeling on the stomach wall flat-mounts.

substeps.instruction: Wash stomach walls six times for 5 minutes each in 0.01 M PBS (pH = 7.4).
Block tissues for 4 days in a mixture of 2% bovine serum albumin, 10% normal goat and donkey serum, 2% Triton X-100, and 0.08% NaN3 in 0.01 M PBS (pH = 7.4).
Incubate with primary antibody (1:1000 dilution) for 4 days in a solution of 2% bovine serum albumin, 4% normal goat and donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100, and 0.08% NaN3 in 0.01 M PBS (pH = 7.4).

steps.title: Mount and Clear Tissues
steps.instruction: Mount the labeled stomach walls on slides and prepare for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Mount flat-mounts on glass slides and flatten with lead weights (6.75 kg) for 4 hours.
Air-dry under a fume hood for 1 hour.
Dehydrate through ascending ethanol concentrations (75%, 95%, 100%, and 100%) for 4 minutes each.
Clear tissues using xylene for 20 minutes.
Apply DEPEX mounting medium and cover slips.
Air dry slides overnight in a fume hood.

steps.title: Image Acquisition
steps.instruction: Use fluorescence and confocal microscopy to capture images of SP-IR axons and FG-labeled neurons.

substeps.instruction: Survey labeling quality using an Eclipse 80i microscope (20X and 40X lenses).

Acquire whole ventral/dorsal wall images using a TCS SP5 Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope: use HeNe laser (543 nm) for SP-IR axons, ArKr laser (488 nm) for background autofluorescence, and 405 nm laser for FG-labeled neurons.
Scan whole stomach using 20X oil immersion objective (Z-step: 1.5 μm).
Scan regions of interest at high magnification using 40x oil immersion objective (zoom: 1.5 X, Z-step: 1 μm).
Image FG-labeled flat-mounts using an Axio Imager M2 with 350 nm excitation wavelength.

steps.title: Image Processing and Density Analysis
steps.instruction: Assemble montages and calculate axon density to create heatmaps.

substeps.instruction: Assemble confocal projection images into montages using ImageJ/Fiji 1.8.0 and Adobe Photoshop 2020.
Import montages into Photoshop and apply a sampling grid with window sizes of 1067x1067 pixels.
Export windows as .png files and use Icy software to calculate 'all signals' (low threshold) and 'axon signals' (high threshold) pixel counts.
Calculate axon density per window in Excel: axon density = nerve signal pixels / surface area pixels.
Reconstruct an overall density montage and apply conditional formatting (Green = Low, Red = High) to create a heatmap.
Isolate the myenteric plexus by cutting out non-plexus areas in Photoshop to create a specific plexus heatmap.
Subtract the myenteric plexus heatmap from the overall heatmap to determine muscular layer density.
